notes: Built from the 1815 map, adjusted to 1848.
The United States after Texas (1845), Oregon (1846) and the Mexican Cession (1848).
Spanish America was independent: Mexico, Central America and South America.
Brazil was an independent empire (1822).
The Dominican Republic broke from Haiti in 1844.
Belgium independent (1830); Greece independent (1832).
Serbia was an autonomous principality under Ottoman suzerainty.
France had conquered Algeria (1830–1847).
Kraków was annexed by Austria in 1846.
Muhammad Ali's Egypt had conquered the Sudan (1820–22).
Russia had taken Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and the Kazakh steppe.
The Sikh Empire was annexed only in 1849.
Sindh (1843), Arakan and Tenasserim (1826) were British.
The Marathas were defeated in 1818; their lands were British or princely states.
Britain claimed all of Australia and New Zealand (1840).
Cape Colony, Natal and the Orange River Sovereignty were British; Boers held the Transvaal.
Liberia declared independence in 1847.
Filled gaps in the source map from the nearest map (within 50 years).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
"Malaya" is a British-era name; the peninsula and its neighbours were Malay sultanates.
Somalia is a 20th-century state; the region was held by Somali sultanates and clans.
The Canary Islands were conquered by Castile by 1496; the Guanche territory is Castilian/Spanish here.
The Kingdom of Benin and the Niger delta were labelled "Sotho", a people of southern Africa; the land west of it was labelled "Africa".
Territories filed under the wrong realm are moved to their own (for example the islands of South-East Asia, Travancore and Cochin, Cochin China, Sardinia).
Names are the ones in use on this map’s date.
Two different states with one name are named apart (for example the Kingdom of Kongo and the modern Congo).
States drawn after they ended, or before they began, are replaced by what held the land on this map’s date.
